solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cook a lot topping Italy's pasta

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the later one

parts.note: to cook the books is to rig or falsify them
a ton is informally a great deal
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A recipe line: make plenty of Italian pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is not about the kitchen here: it means rig, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbed tubes of durum wheat are one familiar shape among the many kinds of Italian noodle.

parts.note: belonging to the man is his
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A man's petty, needling taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hissing at a performer is a classic sound of contempt meant to goad or mock.

indicators.note: the words Lovers usually hold the run of letters within them, as if hugging it

explanation.surface: Romantic partners commonly cuddling while fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' fits the sports-fixture sense: Arsenal playing Spurs is Arsenal against Spurs.
explanation.definitionFit: On a fixture list one side playing another is set against it, the Latin preposition of opposition.

clue.text: Caesar's heart found in morgue, horribly macabre

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are twisted into a dreadful new shape
the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle pair of the Roman's name

parts.note: taken as written as part of the pool to rearrange

explanation.surface: The dictator's heart turns up in a mortuary, a ghastly discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives ES, the middle two letters of CAESAR; 'horribly' mixes ES with MORGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something grim and ghastly, dwelling on death and horror; they are near synonyms.

indicators.note: blows is read as a verb, the letters being blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Stand tall again after taking devastating punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering blows' reads as a boxer's beating; 'blows' is actually the verb rearranging SHATTERING, and 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up from a crouch or bend is to unbend the body and stand erect, so the two phrases match.

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, and the possessive adds an S
a cot is a small bed, especially a child's

explanation.surface: A lucky trinket belonging to the master's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: MA, Master of Arts, is a standard abbreviation for a master.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's or person's lucky emblem is a good-luck token, a charm in the talisman sense.

clue.text: Craft with single course facing empty seas

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a line is a course or route taken

indicators.note: empty means take out the contents, leaving only the outer letters of the word seas

explanation.surface: A lone boat setting a course across a barren sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft here is guile or cunning, the abstract quality of being artful and sly.

clue.text: Is raised by practically strict nun

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word Is is read upwards, backwards
practically means almost all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: stern means strict, severe

explanation.surface: A severe nun is promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' drops the last letter of STERN, the synonym of 'strict', leaving STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a religious order is addressed by this title, so it is a direct synonym.

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel; the 's stands for is, a link
to tan someone is to thrash them

explanation.surface: A rogue is struck, receiving a caning.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing palm's stems are used as canes, for furniture and for punishment sticks.

clue.text: Progress made by the old man's son

parts.note: the old man is father, pa, and the possessive adds an S
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Advancement achieved by the father's boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to move on or advance, as in passing to the next stage; the verbs coincide.

indicators.note: stocking means holding something inside, as a shop stocks goods
terrible suggests the letters of the word are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A dreadful works canteen stocks American grub.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive's S counts as fodder here; 'Terrible' makes STENANCE, and 'stocking' is the shop sense of holding goods, so the jumble holds US.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment of any kind keeps the body going, so a formal word for nourishment is a synonym of food.

indicators.note: for speakers means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: hoards are collections or stockpiles of treasure

explanation.surface: Musical groups assembling collections for loudspeakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' looks musical but means crowds; 'speakers' hints at audio equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Large unruly groups of people, a horde of fans, are bands in the sense of gangs.

parts.note: read as a stay-at-home refusing to go out, but it means declining to bequeath property, cutting an heir out of a will

explanation.definitionFit: To deny an heir an inheritance is to refuse to leave them property, the house included.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Smear a little caramel over the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen or stretch something out is to spread it further, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Upset since originally trapped in fly, perhaps

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
originally points to the first letter of trapped

explanation.surface: Distressed since being caught in a fly-trap, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly is one example of a small six-legged creature, hence the 'perhaps'.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: taking means the hurry word swallows another piece

parts.note: haste is hurry, a rush
one is I, and one's is I's, giving IS

explanation.surface: A cold dash as part of one's training.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish or rebuke someone is to discipline them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Explosive dissolved before detonator's top fired

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: HE is high explosive
acid ate away the metal: ate means corroded or dissolved

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Explosive melted before the detonator's cap went off.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln or furnace that is fired up has been heated; the two past participles match.

clue.text: In need, hurried to acquire record by Queen

indicators.note: to acquire means the hurry word takes the others inside it

parts.note: dived means rushed, as in dived into a shop
an EP is an extended-play record
R is Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Short of cash, rushing to get a Queen single.
explanation.definitionFit: People lacking basic necessities are needy, so the adjective matches the phrase.

indicators.note: lifting means removing, and middle names the central letter of the word for guts

parts.note: bellies are stomachs, guts

explanation.surface: Hiding one's paunch by sucking in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: If something belies a fact it gives a false impression of it, so it disguises it.

clue.text: Cut both sides of tree sheltering last animal

indicators.note: sheltering means the outer letters enclose the rest
both sides of means the first and last letters of tree

parts.note: to last is to run, as a play runs or lasts for months
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Fell a tree on both sides, protecting the last creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something by lopping off part of it is to cut it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Staggered about dinghy's prow catching fish

indicators.note: catching means the outer pieces close around the fish

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an eel is a fish

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so the first letter

explanation.surface: Lurched round the dinghy's bow while landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or lurch unsteadily, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Continental appetiser nibbled at party events initially

definitions.text: Continental appetiser nibbled at party events initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A French starter is nibbled at drinks parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury on bread, of French origin, is the archetypal party appetiser.

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is docked, losing the last letter

parts.note: a vase is a vessel; the 's means is, a link

explanation.surface: A container ship is in port, with its sails furled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails are made of heavy cloth, so the material stands for the sails themselves.

indicators.note: boils suggests the letters seethe and churn into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner carries on despite having painful boils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boils' looks like a noun for sores but is the verb churning RANDESPITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone walking rather than riding is going on foot, so the word works as a modifier.

parts.note: kit means gear, equipment

explanation.surface: Changing using second gear while driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic act on stage is a turn in variety-show language.

clue.text: Beneath ocean is large marine creature

indicators.note: beneath places the large letter under the ocean word in this down clue

parts.note: the sea is the ocean

explanation.surface: Below the waves is a big sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flippered mammal of coastal waters is a marine creature, a straightforward example.

indicators.note: around means the ship letters go about the lake

parts.note: SS is steamship
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Oars pull a ship across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence of things in order, like rows of seats, is a set or run of them.

clue.text: Sailor one predicts sheltering at a distance

indicators.note: sheltering means the prophet word encloses the other piece

parts.note: a seer is one who predicts the future
afar means at a distance

explanation.surface: A mariner who forecasts, protecting things far away.
explanation.definitionFit: One who travels by sea is a mariner, a synonym for sailor.
